title: Term Life Insurance Waiver Charge Base by Issue Age: Quarterly Billing Conversion
content:
In the converted quarterly installment of a Term Life Insurance policy — the installment set when the policy is converted to quarterly direct billing after its monthly bank-draft privilege ends — the waiver charge base, to which the waiver rate is applied when the waiver of premium rider is attached, is chosen by the insured's issue age (whole years from the insured's date of birth to the issue date on record):

| Issue age | Waiver charge base |
|---|---|
| 40 or more | the face premium plus the accidental death charge plus the children's term charge |
| 30 through 39 | the face premium plus the accidental death charge |
| below 30 | the face premium alone |

### Basis Q&A

**Does the children's term charge enter the base of an insured issued at 39?** No. At 39 the base is the face premium plus the accidental death charge; the children's term charge enters only from issue age 40.

**What is the base for an insured issued at 30 with no accidental death rider?** The face premium plus the accidental death charge, which is nothing on that policy, so the base equals the face premium.

**Hypothetical figures:** face premium 360.00, accidental death charge 96.00, children's term charge 33.00. Issue age 42: base 489.00. Issue age 33: base 456.00. Issue age 27: base 360.00.
